the Congo is following very closely the

Africa, a continent at the center of uh
many UN challenges and global
geopolitical issues must remain at the

of the Congo, restoring trust and
managing transformation

resonates as a call for clarity and

has never needed um renewed, inclusive

a legitimate right
grounded
which reflects the realities of the 21st

quote the following. our contribution to
supporting Namibia's liberation and then
the withdrawal of Cuban troops from
Angola through the 1988 Brazville
protocol, the efforts to end hostilities
in the Central African Republic, the
initiatives to promote reconciliation in
Libya where my country leads the African
Union High Level Committee.
also the peace efforts in the Great
Lakes region. Our diplomacy is not a
diplomacy of confrontation. It is
diplomacy based on dialogue, mediation,
mutual respect, and African solutions to
African problems.
We reaffirm here and now the pan-African
vocation about diplomacy and our
commitment to international law. Your
excellencies, ladies and gent gentlemen,
sovereignty is not a rejection of
cooperation. Sovereignty is the ability
of a people and a nation to freely
determine their priorities, to defend
their legitimate interest, to choose
their partners, and to preserve their
independence in decision-m.
This is the understanding of sovereignty
that the Republic of the Congo upholds
and we intend to continue pursuing a
foreign policy based on non-alignment,
diversification of partnerships, mutual
respect among states and the rejection
of any foreign interference in domestic
affairs. We are open to the world, but
we intend to remain masters of our
choices and our destiny.
The Republic of the Congo does not seek
to choose one camp against another.
Rather, we seek to be a bridge between
nations. Your Excellencies, ladies and
gentlemen, the Republic of the Congo has
embarked upon a profound transformation
through our national road map which is
called Let's Accelerate the March
towards Development and it includes the
following priorities. Investing in human
capital, promoting youth employment,
strengthening public governance,
diversifying the economy, modernizing
agriculture and industry, expanding
infrastructure, accelerating digital
transformation and innovation, and
consolidating peace and social cohesion.
We are building a Congo that does more
than export raw materials. We aim to
process and add value to our resources
domestically. And this explains our
interest in special economic zones
because we think political sovereign so
sovereignty must go hand inhand with
economic sovereignty.
Our vision
I would like to point out align with the
sustainable development goals,
the SGS and the 2063 African Union

lucid and pragmatic here. The ambitions
of our development at the Republic of
the Congo and many other African

failure. The Republic of the Congo
therefore calls for an ambitious

developing country debt, including
through debt relief and where
appropriate debt cancellation measures
to free resources for SG related

and gentlemen,
Africa is not the world's periphery. It

advances the international agenda and

Africa contributes towards defining the

will continue with its commitment to
Africa. The uh removal of the visas um
as of the 1st of January 2027 for
Africans
promotes free movement, interffrican

making our
trade more inclusive

Luango must become a place of truth.
remembers reflection but also a place of

should become a bridge between Africa

The the people of African descent

can reconnect with a history, identity

Your excellency, ladies and gentlemen,
we also reaffirm
our determination to mobilize congalles

benefit, an intellectual one, scientific
and economic one. Its competencies, its
experience, its investments, commitment
are needed to accelerate our own
development. We need all of our children
for to realize our human capital. The
Republic of the Congo is a land of
opportunity. It's endowed with natural

potential, which has not yet been
developed. our expanding infrastructure
and a strategic location at the heart of
central Africa. And we invite investors
and development partners to join us
through uh for example mutually
beneficial public private partnerships.
We want the partnerships that create
added value, develop our national
competencies, promote technology
transfer, respect our interests, and
help us manage and develop our economy.
Your excellencies, ladies and gentlemen,
the Republic of the Congo also bears a
special responsibility for the Congo
basin, which is the world's second
largest environmental lung. This
exceptional uh ecosystem
contain contains immense biodiversity
and plays a crucial role in regulating
the global climate. The Congo basin is
one of Africa's principal contributions
to the fight against climate change. We
cannot continuously accept uh that
countries preserve these ecosystems on
their own and bear the cost alone.
Conservation has a cost and
international solid solidarity must also
have a value. We therefore call for fair
and predictable compensation for
ecosystems and carbon services, for
innovative sustainable financing
mechanism, increased capitalization of
the blue fund, and for the recognition
of the Congo basin as a global priority
and with the strengthening of
international cooperation aimed at
preserving it.
We
support
a United Nations institution in the
Republic of the Congo um dedicated to
the preservation of the basin.
We also are asking for a launching of a
decade of the United Nations on a
forestation, reforestation and national

Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen. Um,
above and beyond our rivers and forests,
the tourist of the territory of the
country is more than a geographical
space. It is the foundation of our
nation, the basis of our identity, the
territory for our sovereignty. The
Republic of the Congo will always defend
the integrity of its territory, the
security of our borders, mastering our
resources, and the freedom of our

not negotiable. It is the responsibility

ladies and gentlemen,
we are a defender of peace

call for negotiations between Russia and

surrender, that dialogue is not

will continue to prioritize mediation,
dialogue, and looking for peaceful
political solutions so as to build
Africa which is prosperous and in peace.
From Libya to Sahel, from Sudan to Great
Lakes, we reiterate the fact that we are
available to accompany our brotherly
countries in their work to achieve
return to peace and stability.
Throughout history, we know that peace
is difficult to build, but it is the
only victory that benefits one and all.
Ladies and gentlemen, your excellency,
guided by the same sense of
responsibility, the recurring Ebola
outbreaks and repeated pandemics have
shown that global threats are no longer
solely military or economic. Health
security has become an essential
component of collective security. And
here
we will continue supporting
the strengthening of the World Health
Organization regional office for Africa
in Brazil and will shoulder all of its
responsibilities in accordance with the
1952 headquarters agreement. We also
call for international governance of
artificial intelligence and outer space.
These technologies must remain in the
service of humanity, progress and the
empowerment of peoples.
Technological progress must not become a
new instrument of domination. Africa
must also be a center of creativity,
innovation, and digital sovereignty.
Your Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen,
to conclude,
the Republic of the Congo remains
faithful to its principles, peace,
development, sovereignty, good
neighborliness, dialogue, cooperation,
and mutual respect amongst nations. We
will continue to defend our national
interests while fulfilling our
international responsibilities.
We will continue to believe in Africa
and in our shared destiny. and we will
continue to choose the United Nations as
a privileged space for dialogue amongst
people. I thank you.
